Chethan's Recomp Plan

Progression

Month by month

Six body-part days, each area trained about twice a week: chest (Mon, Fri), back (Tue, Fri), legs (Wed, Sat), shoulders (Thu), arms (Mon, Tue, Thu), core (Wed, Fri, Sat). Each session: 8–10 min warm-up, the lifts, the finisher, 5 min stretch. The exercises mostly stay the same; the weights, reps and sets go up. That is what builds muscle and burns fat.

The one rule: when you hit the top of the rep range on every set (for example 3 × 12), add weight next session: 2.5 kg on dumbbells, 5 kg on machines and barbells. Reps drop back to 8, then build up again.
Month 1

Foundation

Weeks 1–4
Training
Weeks 1–2: 2 sets of everything, light, learn the form. Weeks 3–4: full 3 sets, start adding weight with the rule above.
Cardio
Finishers as written. Bike: 15 min steady in weeks 1–2, intervals (30 s hard / 90 s easy × 6) from week 3.
Food
~1,850 kcal, 130 g protein. Learn the meal-prep routine.
Steps
8,000 a day
Check
InBody at the end of week 4
Target
−2.5 to −3 kg · waist tighter · lifts feel smoother
Month 2

Build

Weeks 5–8
Training
Same exercises, heavier every week using the rule. Weeks 7–8: add a 4th set to exercise 01 each day.
Cardio
Bike intervals go to × 8 rounds. Treadmill incline up to 10–12%.
Food
If the Sunday weight stays flat 2 weeks in a row, cut 150–200 kcal (half a cup less rice at dinner).
Steps
9,000 a day
Check
InBody at the end of week 8
Target
−5 to −6 kg total · body fat ~33% · clothes fit looser
Month 3

Level up

Weeks 9–12
Week 9
Deload: same exercises, half the sets, about 70% of your weights. Recover. Retest blood (vitamin D, B12, lipids, uric acid) this week.
Weeks 10–12
8 exercise swaps (below). First two exercises each day: 4 sets × 6–10, heavier. The rest stay 3 × 10–12.
Cardio
Every finisher +5 min. Bike intervals × 8–10.
Food
Recalculate from the week-9 InBody, likely ~1,750 kcal, protein stays 130 g.
Steps
10,000 a day
Target
−7 to −9 kg total · body fat 30–31% · visceral fat 11–12

Month 3 exercise swaps · weeks 10–12

New movements so your body keeps adapting. Sets, reps and rest follow the Month 3 rules above.

Meal prep

Cook twice a week

Cooked food keeps 3 days in the fridge, so prep happens on Sunday evening and Wednesday night. Portion everything into boxes as soon as it cools. Each day, only the rice is cooked fresh (10 min in the cooker), plus a 5-minute egg or paneer bhurji on some nights.

Sunday, 6 PM · for Mon–Wed

  • Boil 12 eggs (kept unpeeled, they last the week)
  • Dal, 4 portions
  • Soya chunks curry (50 g dry), 1 portion
  • Chicken curry (450 g), 3 portions
  • Palya (beans or cabbage), 3 days
  • Sprouts: soak moong Saturday night, sprouted by Sunday, lasts 3 days

Wednesday night · for Thu–Sat

  • Rajma or chana curry, 2 portions
  • Paneer capsicum masala (100 g), 1 portion
  • Chicken sukka (450 g), 3 portions
  • Dal and palya, 3 days
  • Optional: freeze half and thaw in the fridge the night before

Buy ready, save time

  • Idli / dosa batter
  • Phulkas from a local chapati shop
  • Curd and buttermilk packets
  • Roasted chana and peanuts
  • About 10 steel or glass boxes
  • Prep day missed? A Darshini meal with an extra egg or chicken side, no fried items

Food

Diet rules that do the work

Daily targets

  • ~1,850 kcal. About 450 below what you burn with 6 gym days and a desk job. Expect 0.5–0.75 kg loss a week.
  • 130 g protein on non-veg days, ~100 g on veg days. Protein in every meal.
  • Plate: half vegetables, a quarter protein, a quarter rice/roti/ragi.
  • Oil: 3 teaspoons total for the whole day. Rotis without ghee.
  • Dairy: no milk (lactose). Curd, buttermilk and paneer are fine.
  • Water: 3–3.5 litres. Buttermilk counts. Important for your uric acid.
  • Seed mix: 1 tbsp flax + pumpkin seeds at breakfast, daily.
  • Fresh breath: no raw onion or garlic. Cook curries with tomato, ginger, hing and curry leaves; a little well-cooked onion only if it doesn't bother you. Saunf after meals.
  • 8,000+ steps daily, including Sunday.

Cut these out

  • Milk tea and coffee: drink them black, no sugar
  • Fruit juices, cool drinks, packaged snacks, bakery items
  • Fried food (bajji, vada, chips): once a week at most
  • Eating out: once a week, Sunday lunch is your relaxed meal
  • Late dinners: finish by 8:30 PM so you sleep well before the 5 AM alarm
  • Alcohol: if you drink, keep it to one occasion a week

Portions

  • 1 cup rice = cooked, about 150 g
  • Rotis = 2 shop-bought phulkas
  • Chicken = 150 g raw, palm-sized
  • Soya chunks = 50 g dry (one fistful)
  • Dal = 1 bowl (about 30 g dry)
  • Peanuts = 20 g, a small handful

Before every workout

Daily warm-up

8–10 minutes, Monday to Saturday. Do W1–W8 every day, then the two add-ons for that day. Skip long 30-second stretches before lifting; keep those for after.

DayAdd-on W9Add-on W10
Warm-up sets on the first exercise only: 1 set × 12 at about half your working weight, then 1 set × 6 at about 70%. These don’t count toward your 3 sets.
